meta.title: Slide Template Guide
meta.description: Introduction to available layouts and components

content.title: Slide Template Guide
content.subtitle: Introduction to available layouts and components Place public/slides.json to customize

notes.speakerNotes:
This presentation introduces how to use slide templates.
You can freely customize slide content by placing public/slides.json.
summary: Introduction to the slide template guide

left.heading: Left Column: heading
paragraphs: Write body text with paragraphs. HTML tags are also supported.
You can specify multiple paragraphs using an array.

items: Ideal for displaying code or hierarchical structures

notes.speakerNotes: This slide explains the basic structure of the two-column layout. The left column contains heading, paragraphs, and items, while the right column has codeBlock, titledBulletList, and accentText.

paragraphs: Specify component in left / right to embed registered visuals.

notes.speakerNotes: You can embed registered components by specifying a component field in the left or right columns of a two-column layout.

content.title: layout: "content" — Timeline (steps)

steps.title: Step Title
steps.description: No limit on the number of steps

content.footer: footer: Display supplementary text below the timeline

notes.speakerNotes: When you specify steps in a content layout, it displays in timeline format. Each step requires number, title, and description. command is optional.

tiles.title: Icon: Description
tiles.description:
Specify icon names in the icon field.
Icons registered in registerDefaults are available.

tiles.title: Icon: PlaylistAddCheck
tiles.description:
HTML tags like
<br/> and <code> are supported in description.

tiles.title: Icon: Traffic
tiles.description: Tiles are displayed in a 3-column grid. You can place 2 or 3 tiles.

notes.speakerNotes: When you specify tiles in a content layout, it displays in a tile grid format. Each tile has icon, title, and description.

content.title: layout: "content" — Component (component)
content.footer: Content layout components are rendered inside a wrapper with a title bar

notes.speakerNotes: When you specify component in a content layout, the component is rendered inside a ContentLayout wrapper with a title bar. It is treated as a child element of the content layout, similar to steps and tiles.

content.title: layout: "bleed" — Full-width Two-column
content.titleDescription: titleDescription: Display title supplement in left column

commands.text: ✓ You can specify color for each line

notes.speakerNotes: The bleed layout displays in a full-width two-column format. The left column contains title, titleDescription, and commands, while the right column holds a component.
summary: Right: component for any registered component

notes.speakerNotes: The custom layout renders the specified component directly. Unlike the content layout, there is no wrapper such as a title bar, and the component occupies the entire slide.
summary: Understand the difference from content layout

paragraphs: The Image component displays images, with an automatic fallback on load errors.

notes.speakerNotes: The Image component wraps FallbackImage and shows a fallback UI when image loading fails. Specify src, width, and height in props.
summary: Specify src, width, height in props

titledBulletList.title: TerminalAnimation
items: logTextUrl: URL of the log file e.g., "/demo-log.txt"
Uses built-in default when logTextUrl is omitted

right.accentText: → Use icon names in the tiles icon field of content layout

notes.speakerNotes: This is a list of components registered by default. TerminalAnimation and 5 MUI icons are available.

paragraphs: Place components in addons/src/ to dynamically register and use them in slides.

items.description: Addons are registered to ComponentRegistry at startup

right.accentText: → addons/ is gitignored and only works locally

notes.speakerNotes: The addon system allows you to add custom components. Place an entry file in addons/src/ and register it with window.__ADDON_REGISTER__.
The meta field lets you set transition, background color, background image, and speaker notes for each slide. The theme field configures colors and fonts for the entire presentation.
summary: theme: colors, fonts for entire presentation
notes can be string or object format

right.heading: Two Ways to Set Theme
right.accentText: → All colors have -rgb variants (usable with rgba())

notes.speakerNotes: Theme colors can be set via slides.json theme.colors or public/theme-colors.json. Custom CSS can also be specified with customCSS. All colors automatically generate -rgb variants.
Set a logo image with meta.logo. Specify the path with src and the size with width / height. The logo is not displayed when meta.logo is omitted.
summary: No logo is shown when omitted

left.heading: meta.confidential
left.headingDescription: Show a Confidential watermark across the deck

items.description: Override logo and confidential per slide

notes.speakerNotes: Set a deck-wide Confidential watermark with meta.confidential. text is required, and anchor / offset control the position while opacity / rotate adjust the look. You can override logo and confidential per slide with slides[].meta.confidential and slides[].meta.logo, including hiding just the logo with hidden: true.
summary: Show a deck-wide watermark with meta.confidential
Override logo/confidential per slide with slides[].meta

items.description: Array of external font URLs (e.g., Google Fonts)

notes.speakerNotes: Customize font families with theme.fonts. Three types can be specified — heading / body / code — along with baseFontSize for the base size and sources for external font URLs.

left.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Click the "Presenter View" button in the top right to open a dedicated presenter window.
The main window and presenter view are synchronized bidirectionally. You can navigate slides from either window.

right.accentText: → Set speakerNotes and summary in meta.notes to make the most of it

notes.speakerNotes: The presenter view opens in a separate window and is synchronized bidirectionally with the main window. You can navigate slides from either window.
summary: Opens in separate window via top-right button

items.description: Displays speaker notes (speakerNotes) for the current slide
Shows a thumbnail of the previous slide
Shows a thumbnail of the next slide
Displays summary points as bullet list

notes.speakerNotes: The presenter view shows 4 panels: speaker notes, previous/next slide previews, and key points summary. Use ←/→/Space to navigate from either window.
summary: 4 panels: speaker notes, prev/next previews, summary

right.heading: Toolbar Buttons

items.description: Manually play or stop the current slide's audio
Toggle automatic audio playback on slide transition
Toggle automatic slide advance when audio ends

right.accentText: → Auto-play + Auto-slideshow enables fully automated presentations

notes.speakerNotes: This slide introduces the audio playback feature. Specify the audio file path in meta.notes.voice to enable playback from the toolbar. Combining auto-play and auto-slideshow enables fully automated presentations across all slides.
summary: Toolbar controls: manual play, auto-play, auto-slideshow
Auto-play + auto-slideshow for fully automated presentations

content.title: layout: content (body/items)
content.body: When none of steps / tiles / component are specified, body and items render plain body text.

items.text: Child items can have their own items

notes.speakerNotes: When none of steps / tiles / component are specified, body and items render plain body text. items support emphasis and can be nested.
summary: items support emphasis: true for bold text

notes.speakerNotes: Specifying images on the content layout arranges multiple images in a grid. Each image can set src, alt, and caption.
summary: images renders multiple images in a grid
Set src, alt, and caption per image
Landscape, portrait, and square images align consistently

notes.speakerNotes: The "Diagram" component freely places cards (nodes), connectors, arrows, badges, and callouts using normalized coordinates (0-1). Arrows can be dashed via dashed: true, and solid lines get a continuous flowing light effect.
summary: The Diagram component places diagram primitives
Coordinates are normalized (0-1) relative to the canvas

notes.speakerNotes: chart.type: "bar" renders a vertical bar chart. Specify multiple series to compare them side by side. Bars grow upward on appearance.
summary: chart.type: "bar" renders a vertical bar chart
Multiple series render side by side for comparison

notes.speakerNotes: chart.type: "line" renders a line chart, including dense time-series data such as monthly trends. Lines draw in from left to right.
summary: Multiple series compare, e.g., actual vs. plan

notes.speakerNotes: chart.type: "pie" renders a pie chart, ideal for showing proportions, with the legend generated automatically below. Slices pop in from the center.
chart.type: "hbar" renders a horizontal bar chart, staying readable even when category names are long.
summary: chart.type: "hbar" renders a horizontal bar chart
Best when category names are long
Row spacing auto-adjusts for many categories

notes.speakerNotes: chart.type: "kpi" shows a large number with a trend sparkline. Use label, value, and delta to highlight a key metric.
summary: chart.type: "kpi" shows a large value with a trend
Specify label, value, delta, and trend
The sparkline draws in from left to right

notes.speakerNotes: Passing multiple items to chart.type: "kpi" lays out a row of KPIs. Font size automatically shrinks as the count grows.
summary: items lays out multiple KPIs in a row
Font size auto-shrinks as the count grows

notes.speakerNotes: Specifying table on the content layout renders a table with borders and zebra striping. Rows appear from top to bottom, and each column can set its own alignment.
summary: table renders a table with borders and zebra stripes
columns set width and alignment per column

notes.speakerNotes: compare renders two options side by side for comparison. Setting status: "pass"/"warn"/"fail" on each item shows an icon and color for the verdict.
summary: compare shows two options side by side
status: pass/warn/fail sets icon and color

notes.speakerNotes: flow renders a horizontal process flow of cards connected by arrows. Card width and font size auto-adjust to the number of steps.
summary: flow renders a horizontal process flow
Width and font size auto-adjust to the step count

checklist.title: Acceptance criteria met
checklist.description: Map one-to-one with the issue checkboxes

checklist.title: Reference deck recaptured
checklist.description: Only the added slide types should differ

checklist.title: Visual inspection passed
checklist.description: Zero overflow, safe-area or decoration overlaps

checklist.title: Out-of-scope work written up
checklist.description: File follow-up issues and cite the numbers

notes.speakerNotes: checklist renders a list of items with checkboxes. Set checked: true to mark an item as complete.
summary: checked: true marks an item as done

steps.title: Migrate the base
steps.description: Move private rules to the shared contract

steps.title: Verify by measuring
steps.description: Detect overflow from the real DOM

notes.speakerNotes: Adding stepColumns to steps switches to a multi-column numbered list without a connecting line, which suits timelines with many steps.
summary: stepColumns renders steps in multiple columns
A numbered list without a connecting line
More readable than one row when there are many steps

left.heading: A diagram inside a column
paragraphs: The column itself hands the remaining body height to the canvas

items.text: The column is the fill host
Marking the body area instead breaks the 2-column grid

notes.speakerNotes: Placing the Diagram component in a two-column's left/right lets the column itself hand its remaining height to the canvas. The height-receiving point must live on the column, not the body area.
summary: Place Diagram inside a two-column's left/right
The column hands its remaining height to the canvas
The fill host must be the column, not the body area

content.quote:
Never bend the design
to save implementation effort

notes.speakerNotes: The center layout's variant: "quote" displays a quotation with its citation prominently. Use it for a strong statement or a closing line.
summary: Best for a strong statement or memorable closing line

content.body: The pale variant, used to switch chapters

notes.speakerNotes: variant: "message" shows one message per slide on a pale background, useful when you want to draw attention, such as a chapter switch.
summary: variant: "message" shows one message per slide
The pale background draws attention to the text

content.message:
Fill the slide
to land the point
content.body: The fill and text colors live in the master and its tokens

notes.speakerNotes: variant: "message-inverse" pairs with a full-bleed master fill to make the point stand out. Fill and text colors live in the master and its tokens, so contrast is verified automatically.
summary: variant: "message-inverse" pairs with a full-bleed fill
Fill/text colors live in the master and tokens

content.body: Closing on a full-bleed fill with the logo behind it

notes.speakerNotes: variant: "closing" is built for the final slide and pairs with a full-bleed logo placement. Specifying githubRepo shows a link to the repository.
summary: variant: "closing" is for the final slide
Pairs with a full-bleed logo placement

notes.speakerNotes: toc renders a table of contents. Specify number, title, and page to list chapter numbers, titles, and starting pages.
summary: Specify number, title, and page per item
Best near the start of a chaptered presentation

notes.speakerNotes: hierarchyDiagram stacks a layered structure (such as an architecture) from top to bottom. Specify title and description on each layer.
serverDiagram groups nodes into zones (such as subnets) and connects them with lines, useful for explaining infrastructure.
orgChart auto-arranges an organization chart just by specifying parent, with no manual layout math needed.
summary: Specify parent to build the hierarchy

notes.speakerNotes: classDiagram renders a UML class diagram. Specify attributes / methods as arrays and use relations for relationships such as inheritance.
summary: classDiagram renders a UML class diagram

notes.speakerNotes: dateTimeline lines up dated milestones on a single line. Specify date, title, and description.
Adding dateTimelineColumns to dateTimeline wraps a long history into multiple columns when there are many entries.
summary: dateTimelineColumns wraps a timeline into columns
Handles long histories with many entries
More compact than a single column

notes.speakerNotes: flowchart places start/end/decision/process nodes using row/col and connects them with edges. shape: "decision" renders a diamond.
summary: flowchart shows a business process flow
shape: start/end/decision/process sets the node kind

notes.speakerNotes: swimlane places process nodes per lane (owner or department) with phases shown as column headers, good for flows where ownership shifts.
summary: swimlane shows a process flow by lane

notes.speakerNotes: gantt shows a schedule using a time axis and task bars. Specify each bar's span with startCol / span.
summary: axis sets the time-axis column headers
startCol / span sets each task's duration

notes.speakerNotes: twoByTwo plots items on a two-axis matrix using x/y coordinates, useful for prioritization such as impact vs. effort.
summary: Best for prioritization, e.g., impact vs. effort

notes.speakerNotes: funnel renders a funnel where each stage's width scales with its value, useful for explaining conversion.
summary: Each stage's width scales with its value

notes.speakerNotes: swot renders the four SWOT quadrants (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats). Specify a bullet list in each quadrant's items.
summary: swot shows the four SWOT quadrants
Set a bullet list in each quadrant's items

notes.speakerNotes: heatmap shows row-by-column values as shading. Set color for the base hue to compare magnitudes at a glance.
summary: heatmap shows row-by-column values as shading
Cells fade in one after another

svg.markup: <svg viewBox="0 0 200 120"><rect x="10" y="70" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="80" y="40" width="40" height="70" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.7" /><rect x="150" y="10" width="40" height="100" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.4" /></svg>
svg.caption: Inlines the SVG markup and follows the theme color via currentColor

notes.speakerNotes: svg inlines the given markup as-is. Using color with currentColor makes the shape follow the theme's color tokens.
summary: color follows theme tokens via currentColor

textDiagram.source:
flowchart LR
  A[Start] --> B{Decision}
  B -->|Yes| C[Done]
  B -->|No| A
textDiagram.caption: Renders Mermaid text-diagram syntax (mermaid loads via dynamic import on first use)

notes.speakerNotes: textDiagram renders a diagram from Mermaid text syntax. Just write the syntax in source to generate flowcharts, sequence diagrams, and more.
summary: textDiagram converts Mermaid syntax into a diagram
Just write the text syntax in source
mermaid loads dynamically on first use

notes.speakerNotes: sequenceDiagram renders message exchanges between lifelines. Use activations to highlight an in-progress span.
summary: lifelines and messages express the exchange

profile.name: Taro Yamada
profile.body:
Building a tool for authoring presentation decks.
Interested in software design and test automation.

notes.speakerNotes: profile renders a profile card with a photo. Specify icon and label in links to line up contact info.
summary: profile shows a profile card with a photo
Specify name, role, org, and body

notes.speakerNotes: Passing labeled groups of images to images displays them grouped with a heading, like partner logos. imageColumns sets the column count per group.
summary: imageColumns sets the column count per group

notes.speakerNotes: meta.backgroundImage sets a background image per slide. To share one across the whole deck, use the image type on theme.masters[].background instead.
summary: meta.backgroundImage sets a per-slide background image
theme.masters[].background (type: image) shares one across the deck
fit: cover/contain and opacity are configurable

content.title: Background image
content.body:
Setting meta.backgroundImage to a path or data URI gives this slide its own background image.
For a more advanced setup shared across multiple slides, set type: "image" on theme.masters[].background instead (fit: cover/contain and opacity are supported).

content.title: layout: "center" (variant: "section")
content.body:
Large title and body text.
You can display a QR code and GitHub link.

notes.speakerNotes: The center layout with variant: section is ideal for section dividers or summary slides with a large title display. You can also place a QR code and GitHub link.
summary: center + variant: section for summary slides
QR code and GitHub link placement
